page_title: RefreshYourMac — Mac cleaner: see what's safe to delete

sources.entry: RefreshYourMac - Mac cleaner that rates every category Safe to Remove, Review, Move to Backup or Protected, and shows what left it behind before anything is deleted. ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: RefreshYourMac
summary.one_liner: A Mac cleaner that scans your disk and rates every category by what cleaning it would cost, from Safe for auto removal to Protected.
keywords: find what to delete on mac
use_cases: Free up disk space on a Mac without deleting something important
Schedule daily automatic cleanup of regenerable files
Clean up Xcode, simulators and package caches as a developer
Fully uninstall an app along with its leftover support files
Monitor free space from the menu bar and clean safe items in one click
summary.what_it_does: Scans a Mac and sorts stored data into four safety levels: Safe for auto removal, Review before deleting, Backup recommended, and Protected. Nothing is deleted until the user approves it or schedules a clean. Scheduled cleaning can run daily or when free space drops below a set floor, and the menu bar shows free space with a Clean All Safe option. It includes seven maintenance jobs such as snapshot thinning and a disk check, each measured first, plus developer-focused categories for Xcode, simulators, package caches and AI coding tool leftovers. It can also uninstall apps along with the support files and caches they left elsewhere.
notable: Four-level safety rating for every scanned category, with a note on what each level costs to clean
Scheduled daily or threshold-based cleaning that only touches auto-removal categories
Developer-focused cleanup for Xcode, simulators and AI coding tool caches
No account required and nothing deleted during a scan
caveats: Requires a paid licence after a 7-day free trial: $14.99 a year, $1.99 a month, or $24.99 one-time
Designed for macOS only; the page names no Windows or Linux version
The 432 GB figure is a single user's reported result on the Mac the app was built on, not a guaranteed outcome
